# aes_gcm - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/aes-gcm/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#rustcrypto-aes-gcm)RustCrypto: AES-GCM

Pure Rust implementation of the AES-GCM
[Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Authenticated_encryption) cipher.

[§](https://docs.rs#security-notes)Security Notes

This crate has received one [security audit by NCC Group](https://web.archive.org/web/20240108154854/https://research.nccgroup.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/NCC_Group_MobileCoin_RustCrypto_AESGCM_ChaCha20Poly1305_Implementation_Review_2020-02-12_v1.0.pdf), with no significant
findings. We would like to thank [MobileCoin](https://www.mobilecoin.com/) for funding the audit.

All implementations contained in the crate are designed to execute in constant time, either by relying on hardware intrinsics (i.e. AES-NI and CLMUL on x86/x86_64), or using a portable implementation which is only constant time on processors which implement constant-time multiplication.

It is not suitable for use on processors with a variable-time multiplication operation (e.g. short circuit on multiply-by-zero / multiply-by-one, such as certain 32-bit PowerPC CPUs and some non-ARM microcontrollers).

[§](https://docs.rs#license)License

Licensed under either of:

at your option.

[§](https://docs.rs#contribution)Contribution

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in the work by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

Simple usage (allocating, no associated data):

```
// NOTE: requires the `getrandom` feature is enabled
use aes_gcm::{
    aead::{Aead, AeadCore, Generate, Key, KeyInit},
    Aes256Gcm, Nonce, // Or `Aes128Gcm`
};
let key = Key::<Aes256Gcm>::generate();
let cipher = Aes256Gcm::new(&key);
let nonce = Nonce::generate(); // MUST be unique per message
let ciphertext = cipher.encrypt(&nonce, b"plaintext message".as_ref())?;
let plaintext = cipher.decrypt(&nonce, ciphertext.as_ref())?;
assert_eq!(&plaintext, b"plaintext message");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#in-place-usage-eliminates-alloc-requirement)In-place Usage (eliminates `alloc` requirement)

This crate has an optional `alloc` feature which can be disabled in e.g.
microcontroller environments that don’t have a heap.

The [ AeadInOut::encrypt_in_place](https://docs.rs/trait.AeadInOut.html#method.encrypt_in_place) and

[methods accept any type that impls the](https://docs.rs/trait.AeadInOut.html#method.decrypt_in_place)

`AeadInOut::decrypt_in_place`[trait which contains the plaintext for encryption or ciphertext for decryption.](https://docs.rs/aead/0.6.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/aead/trait.Buffer.html)

`aead::Buffer`Enabling the `arrayvec` feature of this crate will provide an impl of
[ aead::Buffer](https://docs.rs/aead/0.6.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/aead/trait.Buffer.html) for

`arrayvec::ArrayVec` (re-exported from the [crate as](https://docs.rs/aead/0.6.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/aead/index.html)

`aead`[), and enabling the](https://docs.rs/arrayvec/0.7.7/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/arrayvec/arrayvec/struct.ArrayVec.html)

`aead::arrayvec::ArrayVec``bytes` feature of this crate will
provide an impl of [for](https://docs.rs/aead/0.6.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/aead/trait.Buffer.html)

`aead::Buffer``bytes::BytesMut` (re-exported from the
[crate as](https://docs.rs/aead/0.6.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/aead/index.html)

`aead`[).](https://docs.rs/bytes/1.12.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bytes/bytes_mut/struct.BytesMut.html)

`aead::bytes::BytesMut`It can then be passed as the `buffer` parameter to the in-place encrypt
and decrypt methods:

```
// NOTE: requires the `arrayvec` and `getrandom` features are enabled
use aes_gcm::{
    aead::{AeadCore, AeadInOut, Generate, Key, KeyInit, arrayvec::ArrayVec},
    Aes256Gcm, Nonce, // Or `Aes128Gcm`
};
let key = Key::<Aes256Gcm>::generate();
let cipher = Aes256Gcm::new(&key);
let nonce = Nonce::generate(); // MUST be unique per message
let mut buffer: ArrayVec<u8, 128> = ArrayVec::new(); // Note: buffer needs 16-bytes overhead for auth tag
buffer.try_extend_from_slice(b"plaintext message").unwrap();
// Encrypt `buffer` in-place, replacing the plaintext contents with ciphertext
cipher.encrypt_in_place(&nonce, b"", &mut buffer)?;
// `buffer` now contains the message ciphertext
assert_ne!(buffer.as_ref(), b"plaintext message");
// Decrypt `buffer` in-place, replacing its ciphertext context with the original plaintext
cipher.decrypt_in_place(&nonce, b"", &mut buffer)?;
assert_eq!(buffer.as_ref(), b"plaintext message");
```

#### fn [encrypt_in_place](https://docs.rs#method.encrypt_in_place)(
    &self,
    nonce: &[GenericArray](https://docs.rs/generic-array/0.14.7/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/generic_array/struct.GenericArray.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html), Self::[NonceSize](https://docs.rs/trait.AeadCore.html#associatedtype.NonceSize)>,
    associated_data: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)],
    buffer: &mut dyn [Buffer](https://docs.rs/aead/0.5.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/aead/trait.Buffer.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)>

Encrypt the given buffer containing a plaintext message in-place.

The buffer must have sufficient capacity to store the ciphertext message, which will always be larger than the original plaintext. The exact size needed is cipher-dependent, but generally includes the size of an authentication tag.

Returns an error if the buffer has insufficient capacity to store the resulting ciphertext message.

[Source](https://docs.rs/aead/0.5.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/aead/lib.rs.html#304-309)#### fn [decrypt_in_place](https://docs.rs#method.decrypt_in_place)(

) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)>

#### fn [decrypt_in_place](https://docs.rs#method.decrypt_in_place)(
    &self,
    nonce: &[GenericArray](https://docs.rs/generic-array/0.14.7/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/generic_array/struct.GenericArray.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html), Self::[NonceSize](https://docs.rs/trait.AeadCore.html#associatedtype.NonceSize)>,
    associated_data: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)],
    buffer: &mut dyn [Buffer](https://docs.rs/aead/0.5.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/aead/trait.Buffer.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)>

Decrypt the message in-place, returning an error in the event the provided authentication tag does not match the given ciphertext.

The buffer will be truncated to the length of the original plaintext message upon success.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*
